definition: Recognizing interactions between people — handshake, hug, fight — in images or video, requiring reasoning over multiple bodies rather than individual poses.
details: Recognizing interactions between people — handshake, hug, fight — in images or video, requiring reasoning over multiple bodies rather than individual poses.

explainer.lead: Human interaction recognition identifies interactions between people, such as a handshake, hug, or fight, in images or video. It matters because it requires reasoning over multiple bodies at once rather than treating each pose separately.

tiers.eli5: It looks at two or more people together and tells whether they are shaking hands, hugging, or fighting, instead of just tracking one person.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers model relations across multiple detected people rather than relying on single-person pose estimates. A pitfall is that overlapping bodies and occlusion make multi-person reasoning harder than individual pose detection.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as recognizing interactions between people, such as handshake, hug, or fight, in images or video; it requires reasoning over multiple bodies rather than individual poses.

explainer.example: Given video of two people embracing, the system labels the interaction as a hug by jointly analyzing both bodies.
